This page documents my use of generative AI for
[EPPS 6356 Assignment 3](assignment3.qmd), following the course AI policy.
Logs for the other assignments are on their own pages.

## Tool Information

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| **Tool** | Claude (Anthropic), model `claude-opus-5`, used in the Claude desktop app |
| **Dates** | October 1–2, 2026 |
| **Language** | I asked in Traditional Chinese; the drafted English text and code comments came back in English. |

## How and Why I Used AI

- **Planning:** breaking the five questions into an order I could finish in one
  evening, and explaining what "document a chart" asks for.
- **Checking my understanding of base graphics:** I ran the code myself and wrote
  down what I thought each call did; Claude corrected four of those statements
  (listed below).
- **Reviewing my scripts:** catching errors in the ggplot version before I ran it.
- **Editing my own draft:** tightening the paragraph I wrote for the replication
  question.
- **Assembly:** turning the finished figures and text into `assignment3.qmd`, with
  the figure captions and alt text.

## What Claude Corrected

These are places where I had written something and Claude told me it was wrong:

| My statement | The correction |
|---|---|
| Calling `text()` before `plot()` just does nothing | It raises an error — there is no plot region to draw into yet |
| `plot()` does "a few things" | It does seven: new plot, window, points, axes, box, labels, title |
| My reasoning for why `freq = FALSE` was needed | My reasoning was reversed |
| `boxplot(add = TRUE)` is a low-level function | `boxplot()` is a high-level function being used in a low-level way |

Claude also spotted that a paragraph of English I had typed into
`04_ggplot_version.R` had `##` only on its first line, which would have broken
`source()` on the whole script.

## Editing My Own Writing

For the replication question I wrote a paragraph first and asked Claude to revise
it. The changes it made:

- "linear variance" → "relationship" (I had used a term that does not mean what I
  wanted it to mean)
- "slightly skewed" → "dragged away from it" (the effect is not slight)
- added the concrete detail that **every x value is 8 except one observation at 19**,
  which is the actual reason the fit moves

The argument of the paragraph is mine; the wording above is the edit.

## What Is My Own

- Running every script and producing every figure.
- Choosing which panel of Murrell's chapter 1 to document — I picked the
  scatterplot panel because it is the only one built entirely from `plot.new()`
  and low-level calls.
- The colour choice: I tried several and settled on `magenta3`.
- Deciding to keep the previous week's COVID code for question 5 rather than
  rewrite it under time pressure, and saying so on the page.
- The substance of the replication paragraph.

## A Workflow Problem Worth Recording

When Claude edited `assignment3.qmd` on disk while the file was open in RStudio,
RStudio offered to save its own cached copy over the change. Saving would have
silently reverted the edit. The fix is to choose **Don't Save**, close the tab, and
reopen the file from the Files pane. I mention it because it is the kind of error
that leaves no trace in the output.
